title: How far does the value move when one sign is switched?
description: The expression three plus four minus five minus six is worked out, then one sign is switched at a time, and the two values are compared on the board. Each switch moves the value by twice the number switched, so odd stays odd and even stays even. Keeko raises the doubt that switching a sign changes the value by only the number itself.
teaching_notes: One idea: switching a sign changes the value by twice that number, which is always even, so the parity cannot change. Watch for students who think a switch changes the value by the number alone.

source: Take 3 + 4 − 5 − 6. Switch +4 to −4, then switch −5 to +5 in
video_script.why: A learner sees why switching one sign changes a signed sum by twice that number, and so never changes its parity.
video_script.substitution: the book's own expression: three plus four minus five minus six
video_script.anchor: the expression 3 + 4 − 5 − 6 on sign cards, with one sign card flipped at a time, as in the book
video_script.wrong_answer: changes the value by only four
video_script.wrong_move: thinks switching a sign changes the total by the number itself instead of twice the number
video_script.payoff_line: The value changes by eight and then by ten, and the parity never changes.

final_answer.spoken: the value changes by eight and then by ten, and the parity never changes

maths_rules: each change is 2 times the switched number, so it is even, and an even change keeps odd odd and even even
video_script.design: One idea: the gap between the two values is twice the switched number. Assumes adding and taking away integers. Wrong idea: the change is the number itself. The original expression stays on the board while one sign card flips.

beats.on_screen: title card Switching a Sign; the expression 3 + 4 − 5 − 6 on four number cards with sign cards between them

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the expression is set out in cards
marks.ask: the plus sign before four and the minus sign before five glow in turn
marks.how: a question mark glows over the expression

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about switching signs in three plus four minus five minus six.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Switch the plus before four to minus. Then switch the minus before five to plus, in the original.
<bookmark mark='how'/>How much does the value change each time, and does it stay odd or even?

beats.on_screen: the expression stays on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a sign card flips from + to −; the labels odd and even sit under the number line

marks.switch: one sign card flips from plus to minus and back
marks.parity: the words odd and even appear as one label named parity

narration: <bookmark mark='switch'/>To switch a sign means to change plus to minus, or minus to plus. We do it in front of one number.
<bookmark mark='parity'/>Whether a number is odd or even is called its parity.

beats.on_screen: Given: 3 + 4 − 5 − 6; switch the sign of 4; switch the sign of 5 in the original

marks.given: the expression and the two switches are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the expression is three plus four minus five minus six, and two switches are to be made.

beats.on_screen: To find: the change in value for each switch, and the parity
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how much the value changes each time, and what happens to the parity.

marks.value: the running value ends at minus four and is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='seven'/>Step one, find the original value. Three plus four is seven.
<bookmark mark='value'/>Seven take away five is two. Two take away six is minus four.

marks.switch: the plus before four flips to minus
marks.run: the running value goes to minus one, minus six, minus twelve
marks.gap: the two values minus four and minus twelve are joined by an eight step bracket

narration: <bookmark mark='switch'/>Step two, switch plus four to minus four. Three minus four is minus one.
<bookmark mark='run'/>Take away five and we reach minus six. Take away six and we reach minus twelve.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>The values minus four and minus twelve are eight apart. Eight is two times four.

marks.switch: the minus before five flips to plus in the original
marks.run: the running value goes to seven, twelve, six
marks.gap: the values minus four and six are joined by a ten step bracket

narration: <bookmark mark='switch'/>Step three, switch minus five to plus five in the original. Three plus four is seven.
<bookmark mark='run'/>Seven plus five is twelve. Twelve take away six is six.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>The values minus four and six are ten apart. Ten is two times five.

beats.on_screen: change = 2 × the switched number: 2 × 4 = 8 and 2 × 5 = 10, both even; even change keeps odd odd and even even

marks.twice: both changes are written as two times the switched number
marks.keep: the labels odd and even stay on the same side after an even change

narration: <bookmark mark='twice'/>Step four, each change is two times the number we switched. Two times any whole number is even.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>An even change keeps odd numbers odd and even numbers even. The parity stays the same.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The value changes by eight and then by ten, and the parity never changes.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the expression
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows change = 4, struck through; a number line shows the jump from −12 to −4 as 8 steps, made of two jumps of 4

marks.doubt: the bubble with change four appears
marks.line: the jump from minus twelve to minus four is drawn as eight steps
marks.fix: the jump splits into two jumps of four and the bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks switching the four changes the value by only four.
<bookmark mark='line'/>But on the number line, the jump from minus twelve up to minus four is eight steps.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Plus four becomes minus four, so four is taken away and then four more. That is two times four.
